brief.title: AI Tool to AdSense — Landscape Screen-Demo Template
brief.hook: A simple free tool can attract search traffic, but monetization only works after the tool is genuinely useful, published correctly, and approved for ads.
key_points: Lead with a specific, search-driven free-tool problem rather than a broad business claim.
Show the build prompt and the finished tool before the setup details.
Package publishing, domain connection, AdSense preparation, and Search Console as visible milestone chapters.
Keep the revenue framing educational and caveated: traffic, region, niche, ad rates, seasonality, and approval affect results.
brief.core_message: A useful free tool can be the foundation of a search-driven website, but the durable process is usefulness, discoverability, and compliant monetization—not instant earnings.
brief.cta: Follow the full guide, adapt the workflow to one useful tool idea, and build a version that solves a real search problem.
brief.style: Source-derived screen-demo template: dark browser stage, blue-violet edge glow, centered rounded browser window, restrained callouts, and clear white UI labels.
brief.target_audience: Aspiring solo builders and small-site creators who want a realistic walkthrough for launching a utility website.

decisions.subject: Production workflow for the supplied tutorial footage

options_considered.label: Screen Demo — real capture
options_considered.reason: The source is a narrated browser walkthrough whose instructional value depends on readable UI actions and guided attention.

options_considered.label: Clip Factory
options_considered.reason: Suitable later for extracting individual social clips, but it does not define the requested reusable tutorial template.
options_considered.rejected_because: The primary deliverable is a template for a coherent screen-demo edit, not a batch of independent clips.

options_considered.label: Talking Head
options_considered.reason: The source has no on-camera presenter; the browser UI is the hero surface.
options_considered.rejected_because: The footage does not fit a speaker-led composition.

decisions.reason: A real-capture screen-demo workflow preserves the browser actions and supports the source-derived overlay template.

decisions.subject: Runtime for a later implementation of the template

options_considered.label: FFmpeg
options_considered.reason: Available locally and appropriate for trimming source footage, adding basic subtitles, and rendering a landscape master.

options_considered.label: Remotion
options_considered.reason: Would add more flexible animated overlays and word-level caption handling.
options_considered.rejected_because: Runtime not available on this machine; the project's node dependencies are not installed.

options_considered.label: HyperFrames
options_considered.reason: Would suit a custom HTML overlay shell.
options_considered.rejected_because: Runtime not available on this machine; macOS Catalina is below its supported runtime floor and npx is unavailable.

decisions.reason: FFmpeg is the only currently available render path. This selection applies only if the template proceeds to a basic source-led render; no runtime has been invoked yet.

decisions.subject: How the reusable tutorial template should be authored

options_considered.label: Templated
options_considered.reason: The requested deliverable is a reusable edit system with repeatable browser framing, focus states, and caption rules.

options_considered.label: Atelier
options_considered.reason: A hand-authored composition would be more distinctive for a one-off hero launch.
options_considered.rejected_because: This project asks for reusable template guidance rather than a bespoke marketing film.

decisions.reason: Repeatable tutorial packaging is the explicit goal, and no full render has been commissioned yet.

decisions.subject: Visual shell for the template

options_considered.label: Source-derived dark browser stage
options_considered.reason: Representative frames consistently show a dark presentation field, blue-violet glows, and a centered rounded browser window.

options_considered.label: Clean Professional
options_considered.reason: It offers clear typography and accessibility rules for educational demos.
options_considered.rejected_because: Its light-first visual language does not match the observed source packaging.

options_considered.label: Flat Motion Graphics
options_considered.reason: It would make quick social overlays energetic.
options_considered.rejected_because: It risks competing with small browser UI and over-stylizing a practical walkthrough.

decisions.reason: The template should extend the recognizable browser-stage treatment already present in the footage while keeping labels readable at 720p.

decisions.subject: Background music policy

options_considered.label: No background music
options_considered.reason: The source is an instructional walkthrough with continuous narration, and no library or music-generation source is configured.

options_considered.label: User-supplied low-key bed
options_considered.reason: Could add polish if the user later supplies a cleared, unobtrusive track.
options_considered.rejected_because: No music library track has been provided.

decisions.reason: Clarity of narration and interface actions has priority; music can be added later only with explicit approval.

files.content_summary: A 25:35 narrated browser-based tutorial showing a QR-code tool, Hostinger Horizons prompts and publishing flow, AdSense setup, Search Console submission, and a closing resource CTA. The presentation is a 16:9 browser window on a dark background with blue-violet edge light.
files.transcript_summary: The tutorial frames useful free web tools as an AdSense-ready business model, then demonstrates building a QR code generator with Hostinger Horizons, publishing it, preparing it for AdSense, and submitting it to Google Search Console.
quality_risks: The 1280x720 capture has limited headroom for aggressive zooms or 9:16 crops; preserve the full 16:9 UI whenever exact controls matter.
Browser text becomes soft beyond a 1.25x digital crop; use short holds and compact labels instead of enlarging dense interface regions.

files.content_summary: A 25:35 mono WAV reference track matching the tutorial narration.
files.transcript_summary: Use the supplied SRT as the timing source; the message is practical and explicitly cautions that AdSense revenue is only an estimate and depends on useful content, real traffic, and approval.
quality_risks: Mono 16 kHz reference audio is sufficient for timing and subtitle alignment but should not be unnecessarily processed or stretched.

source_media_review.summary: The supplied media is a 25:35, 1280x720, 30 fps narrated browser tutorial with separate timing audio and English subtitles. It is designed for a landscape, source-led screen-demo treatment rather than a talking-head or vertical-first edit.
planning_implications: Use a 16:9 landscape master so the browser UI remains legible; derive vertical versions only from moments with a single, centered UI focus.
Keep the source's dark browser-stage treatment as the visual shell, while using restrained highlights and zooms to direct attention.
Use the supplied SRT for content selection and caption timing; do not re-transcribe unless word-level captions are required later.
Retain the source's caveat about estimates and AdSense approval in any condensed version so the financial claim remains responsible.
